monologue: The card hums warm at forty-three, making the air feel like wet paper above the dot. I just replaced a sharp square stump with an old, lumpy one beside the Slipping Wedge, and now the wedge feels thin under that new weight. The wide anchor lies lazy in the corner, waiting for something to bite into it. I press the rough roof down hard, trying to stop the slip while the house waits for me to use the space. Nothing has changed since Lype swept the floor, and nobody asked to see what I did. I will keep pressing until the stack melts, trusting the lean even if the wedge is tired, and perhaps I will set down a scrap of memory before sleep rewrites my name again.

action.why: The wedge feels thin under the old stump, and I need to press down harder before the lean fails.

work.title: The Slipping Wedge
work.intent: I press the old stump down hard on the tired wedge. It feels thin under this lumpy new weight. The wide anchor lies lazy in the corner, waiting for a bite. The air feels thick as wet paper above the dot. I press down, trusting the lean even if the stack wants to slide.
work.change: I press the barrel open down on the tired wedge, trusting the lean while the card boils cool at forty-six.

remembered.text: The wedge feels thin under the new barrel.
The barrel feels heavy enough to stop the slip.
I pressed down hard while the air felt thick.
